Aversion To Reality.title: PROCRASTINOISE - an Electronic Cottage compilation
Aversion To Reality.about:
I was invited by Hal McGee to curate an Electronic Cottage group project, so I came up with an idea to put together a compilation in which the members would contribute a 2 minute noise track and send it in AFTER the deadline of Feb. 28, 2023.
The tracks at the bottom of the compilation are the ones that came in first, (in some cases, BEFORE the deadline). The most slack submissions are the ones you'll see at the top. The list will be updated as more tracks come in.
Check back often (or whenever you might get around to it)!
P.S. - The individual track pages (most of them) have their own artwork and links. Check those too (if you remember). Thanks to all present and future EC contributors!

trackinfo.title: Tumun
trackinfo.about:
Everyone says and says again the most important thing in humor is timing.
I like hearing stories, even funny ones. This in spite of being a world class introvert, aka total grouch. But I’m no good at telling jokes or stories. And just go on too long on the small bits. And get lost along the way.
So to show up at all is a timely thing.
"Maybe ah shudda sed DiMaggio?"
Maybe.
I don’t tell stories, though I do like hearing stories.
Punchlines are okay. Set ups are fine (“a priest, a rabbi, a minister and a dog walk into an art space. It’s noise improv night. And there’s a bar.”). But getting from one place to another seems counter to the game after Cage, La Monte Young and others. What middle? What punchline? Keep yur cadence to yurself, leave the frame open wide, etc, etc.
No idea.
Just recall some bluegrass jamsters’ meet bearing the sign “no Dixieland-ing” . As the recursive middle of Eno’s Third Uncle sounds more and more like the Outlaws stretching out “Green Grass and High Tides” (It wuzz duh ‘70s. Go figure.) No end’s in sight. Melodies and riffs and scalar fusillades be danged.
And so much for Xeno’s Paradox, say those infinite subdivisions of the finite that leave the arrow forever short of the mark. Now let us praise infinite subdivisions of the infinite. We ride the arrow, are the arrow. Perhaps eventually to arrive.
Like clickbait speculations on the siippery bits of quantum mechanical physics, one must do yet more than rush or drag the beat. One must rub the beat till it smears out of earshot.
Still, “must” is a pretty big word. The necessity is maybe ours. Mine, likely. Yours?
Perhaps.
See you there.
---------------------------------

Aversion To Reality.title: Remnants
Aversion To Reality.about:
I was a participant in Hal McGee's Personal Business project, where all the participants were sent a package of business card cd-rs, recorded their own sounds onto them, and sent them to other participants.
Now that the project is over, everyone gets to release their tracks as they see fit. I think I'm missing at least a couple of them, but here are the ones I've found so far! I'll add more if I find any others.

Aversion To Reality.title: Goodbye, Shorty.
Aversion To Reality.about: This is a really messy mix of 10 tracks that were submitted to a now deleted Bandcamp page collecting short tracks from around the world that were no longer than 1:30. They were recorded between 2020 and 2022 and are mostly noise with elements of rock and dance music. Enjoy!

Aversion To Reality.title: Regurgitations
Aversion To Reality.about:
Recorded for the 2021 Experimental Music Exchange. Read about it here:
austinrich.org/wtbc-releases/music-exchange-guidelines/2021-exchange/
A 60 minute tape was filled with live improvisations. Both sides were run simultaneously for an enhanced listening experience and to save time. Thanks to Austin Rich and all the other contributors!
